hints: The transformed string is the last column of sorted rotations.
Its sorted characters form the first column of those same rotations.
Match equal characters by occurrence order to move between columns.
analogy: The first and last columns contain the same letters; numbering equal letters links each rotation to the rotation shifted by one character.
example: For transformed cb#ab, the original is babc.
algorithm: Compute each character's occurrence rank in the transformed last column and its starting offset in the sorted first column. This gives the LF mapping from a last-column row to its matching first-column row. Start at the row containing #, repeatedly apply the mapping while collecting last-column characters, and reverse the collected letters, excluding #.
correctness: Stable occurrence matching pairs the same rotations under a one-character cyclic shift. Following LF walks backward through the unique original string, and the sentinel identifies the starting row and where to stop.
complexity: For transformed length n+1 and fixed alphabet, O(n) time and O(n) space.
